subject: lighthouse
pitch: A cozy lighthouse diorama on a tiny rocky island. A red-and-white striped tower with a glowing lantern room and a black iron balcony, a keeper's cottage with a crooked chimney and a blue door, a wooden jetty with a rowboat tied to it, a couple of seagulls, tufts of grass and wildflowers between the rocks, and turquoise water with white foam around the shore, all on a round display base.
reasoning:
I'm planning the module structure with a root joint to anchor the parts, keeping seagull rigging simple rather than fully articulated. I'm also sketching out the diorama's scale, settling on a small base size for the overall model.

Now I'm detailing the individual pieces: a lathed wooden base with turquoise water, a rocky island built from flattened icosahedrons with a grassy top, foam rings near the shore, and a striped lighthouse tower made of stacked cylinders with a gallery, railing, and glowing lantern room using bright emissive-style coloring.

I'm also designing a small cottage on the island with cream box walls and a gabled roof built from an extruded triangular prism, working out the dimensions for width, depth, and overhang.

Now I'm adding details like a blue front door, tiny yellow windows, and a crooked two-box chimney in brick red-brown, then planning where to place a wooden jetty relative to the cottage on the island.

I'm also adding a bench and rope detail to the boat, then planning seagulls with white capsule bodies, orange beak cones, and grey-tipped wings -- one perched on the jetty post, one flying above with a helper function to orient them by yaw.

Adding flowers with stem rods and petal spheres, keeping grass tufts and flower clusters small in part count. For the island itself, I'm shaping a lathe profile defining the rocky base tapering down from the flat grassy top.

I'm coloring the island with a paint function that switches between grass and mottled rock based on surface normal, and using fewer lathe segments for a low-poly faceted look. I'm placing tufts and flowers within a radius while rejecting positions too close to the house and tower footprints.

Now I'm positioning the cottage and tower on the island top, checking their bounding extents against the island radius and making sure the two structures stay far enough apart from each other.

For the tower, I'm laying out its vertical construction: a gray stone foundation, a stack of alternating red-and-white tapering bands, a gallery disc near the top, a loop-generated railing of posts with a torus rail, and a glowing lantern room capping the lighthouse.

Now I'm adding mullions, a dark cone roof, a ball-and-spike finial, and a bright glow inside the lantern. I'm also planning small doors and windows on the tower surface, positioned relative to the tapering radius, and setting up the root joint before starting the lathe profile for the base.

Writing base lathe profile...

I'll make the water a simple cylinder with mottled turquoise paint, and add thin white torus rings for ripples plus a flattened foam torus around the island edge for the shoreline effect.

Now I'm scattering rocks—small icosahedrons with flat shading in gray tones—around the island base and near the water, placed via a randomized loop, then positioning the jetty extending from the island edge outward.

Still writing jetty and boat geometry...

I'll give the boat an orange-ish hull with a cream interior disc near the rim, using a thin cylinder for the inner surface, plus a bench inside -- keeping the hull as an open hemisphere so the cream interior shows through from above.

Working out the rim torus dimensions...

Actually I'll skip the torus rim and just use a slightly lowered cream disc near the hull sphere top for simplicity, no gunwale needed.

Now thinking about gull placement standing on the post top, sizing a small capsule body positioned and scaled appropriately there.

Adding gull head, beak, tail, wings, legs, and eyes...

Now I'm placing two gulls — one perched on a post, one flying nearby with extended wings tapering to dark tips — and working through how frustumBox orients wing width and height along the right axes when the tube runs parallel to world X.

Still figuring out wing orientation...

For folded wings I'll switch to scaled sphere ellipsoids on the sides for simplicity, keeping frustumBox only for flying wings. I'm sketching out tufts of grass blades with varied greens and simple flowers with colored petal spheres and yellow centers, plus a placement helper to scatter ground elements while avoiding overlap near the center.

Now I'm working out rejection zones around the tower and cottage so scattered objects don't spawn inside structures, then moving into cottage construction: a gray stone foundation, cream-colored walls rising to a set height, and a reddish-brown roof on top.

Shaping the roof outline...

I'll add a few small grey spheres rising above the chimney for smoke puffs, keeping the overall palette under the color limit by reusing existing tones. Now I'm setting up the builder script, defining a root joint and a helper function for creating parts with geometry, color, and position shortcuts.

Computing tower geometry...

Now I'm adding the lantern itself—a glowing emissive cylinder with dark mullion strips, topped by a small red conical roof, a dark ring, and a finial ball with a spike for detail.

Writing gull function...

Still defining bird geometry...

Placing a seagull on one of the jetty posts near the boat, figuring out post positions and gull orientation, then working out where to anchor a mooring rope from the post to the boat's bow.

Now I'm laying out the jetty planks and stringers along the z-axis, setting deck height and plank thickness, then sizing the support posts and checking how the jetty meets the island's sloped edge near the grass. Finally I'm getting ready to scatter some flowers randomly across the scene before writing the final output.
